questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Two writers both write about dogs. One text is for Prep children. Which sentence is best for Prep children?
choices: Canines are domesticated mammals that need regular exercise.
Dogs are descended from wolves and vary widely in breed.
A dog can run and jump. It likes to play with you!
Veterinarians recommend annual vaccinations for dogs.
questions.explanation: Prep children are just learning to read. Short sentences and easy words suit them best.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Sam writes about staying safe in the sun. He is writing for Year 6 students, not little kids. Which sentence suits Year 6 best?
choices: Wear a hat, sunglasses and sunscreen, because UV rays can damage your skin.
The sun is a big yellow ball.
Yay, sun! Let us play and play!
questions.explanation: Older students can read longer sentences. This one also gives a reason, which suits their age.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Read this text. "Come to our school fair this Saturday! Win prizes, eat a sausage sizzle and bring your friends!" What is the text trying to do?
choices: Get people to come to the fair
questions.explanation: The exclamation marks and words like "Come" try to make people want to go. That is a persuasive text.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Read this text. "Wally the wombat dug a tunnel all the way to the moon. There he had tea with a kangaroo." What kind of text is it?
choices: Informative, because it gives facts about wombats
Persuasive, because it wants you to dig
Instructions, because it shows how to dig
Imaginative, because it is a made-up story
questions.explanation: A wombat cannot dig to the moon or have tea. The story is made up, so it is imaginative.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Jack grabbed his raincoat and boots. He splashed out the door under his umbrella. What can you work out from this?
choices: It is a hot, dry day.
questions.explanation: Raincoats, boots and umbrellas are used in the rain. The story does not say it, but you can work it out.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Mum asked who broke the cup. Tom went red and hid his hands behind his back. He looked at the floor. How does Tom most likely feel?
questions.explanation: Going red, hiding his hands and looking down are signs of feeling guilty. The text does not say it, so we infer it.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: A syllable is one beat in a word. How many syllables are in the word "kangaroo"?
questions.explanation: Clap it out: kan-ga-roo. That is three beats.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Which shows the word "umbrella" split into syllables the right way?
questions.explanation: Say it slowly and listen for the beats: um-brel-la. There are three syllables.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: A prefix goes at the start of a word. The prefix "un" often means "not". What does "unsafe" mean?
questions.explanation: The prefix "un" means "not". So "unsafe" means not safe.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: A suffix goes at the end of a word. Mia adds "ing" to the word "hop". Which is the correct spelling?
questions.explanation: "Hop" is a short word with one vowel and one end letter. We double the p before adding "ing".

questions.subject: english
questions.explanation: In "knife" the k is silent. The word starts with kn but sounds like n.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Which is the correct spelling of the Australian animal that hops and has a pouch?
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is k-a-n-g-a-r-o-o, with a double o at the end.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Which word fits? "Dad will ___ some bread at the shop."
questions.explanation: "Buy" means to pay for something. "By" and "bye" sound the same but mean other things.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: The words "two" and "too" sound the same but are spelled differently and mean different things.
questions.explanation: Words that sound the same but have different spellings and meanings are called homophones. "Two" and "too" are homophones.
